newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end higher, feeders set new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end higher, feeders set new highs.

text.p: CME live cattle futures ran up to new day's highs late on fund and commercial buying while feeder cattle again posted fresh contract highs on strong cash indications, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.875 to 0.100 cent per lb higher with June pacing the gain at 64.625 cents. Feeder cattle finished 0.225 to 0.575 cent a lb higher with August up 0.350 at 76.350 cents after setting a new contract high of 76.450. September through November and March also posted new contract highs.
Live cattle notched the day's highs late as higher boxed beef values quoted at midday prompted ideas cash cattle may trade at levels steady to stronger than last week, they said.
"Any ideas of stronger cash prices are going to support the June," said Karl Skold, director of research for Frontier Risk Management.

Although cash cattle could trade stronger this week, Skold said he still looked for cattle prices to retreat in the near term on expected larger fed cattle supplies and move discount to futures. Futures currently are well below cash levels, with June futures closing at 64.625 cents and the most recent cash cattle trade reported late last week at $67.00 per cwt.

Some cattle in the Texas Panhandle lost weight in the aftermath of last week's storm. If that sparked a reduction in market-ready cattle this week it could force packers there to raise bids for available supplies, sources said.
Retailer demand for beef is expected to be strong the next few weeks as they book stocks for upcoming May and June holidays, they added.
Cargill Investor Services and R.J. O'Brien bought late while RBH sold June. Refco and ADM Investor Services bought August, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, commercials bought June 67 calls and commission houses sold June 62 and 63 puts. There was also some commercial hedging in August by doing risk reversals, buying 63 puts and selling 67 calls. Volatility was steady to firm, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures climbed to new contract highs despite a drop in the latest CME index and higher corn futures. The index decline was seen as temporary as a large number of Texas direct cattle sales late last week influenced the weighted average index. Cash feeder prices overall were seen steady to higher in the near term, traders said.
"There's still the firm undertone for cash," said Jim Clarkson, analyst for A and A Inc.

The latest CME feeder cattle index slipped $0.83 to $71.95 per cwt. But sources noted that feeder cattle in the key Oklahoma City market traded steady to $2.00 higher Monday. They expect the next index to be quoted higher.

R.J. O'Brien and E.D.&F. Man bought August early and Refco sold late, traders said, and FIMAT Futures USA spread long August/short May. Cargill Investor Services spread long February live cattle/short September feeders and long December live/short August feeders. Stone Traders spread long August feeders/short December live cattle, pit sources said.
